answers.why: Rule 8. The single client is openai.AsyncOpenAI(api_key=config['api_key']) (bot/openai_helper.py:107). That config is the operator dict built once at startup from env OPENAI_API_KEY (bot/main.py:34, 111), not a per-user object, so rule 4 does not apply. There is no base_url (OPENAI_BASE_URL is commented out in .env.example:28, so it defaults to api.openai.com). The model is OPENAI_MODEL/VISION_MODEL, default 'gpt-4o' (main.py:30, 56), a catalog id; there is no state and no beta.

Rule 8. This is the follow-up chat.completions.create after a plugin function call (openai_helper.py:316), on the same env-keyed, default-endpoint client (openai_helper.py:107, main.py:34). model=config['model'] comes from OPENAI_MODEL, default 'gpt-4o' (main.py:30), a catalog id. A config dict passed to __init__ is app config, not a per-tenant key.

Rule 8. This is the vision chat call (openai_helper.py:459) on the same client, keyed by operator env OPENAI_API_KEY (main.py:34), with the default endpoint. model=config['vision_model'] comes from VISION_MODEL, default 'gpt-4o' (main.py:56), a catalog id.

Rule 8. This is the history-summarisation chat call in __summarise (openai_helper.py:612) on the same env-keyed, default-endpoint client. model=config['model'] comes from OPENAI_MODEL, default 'gpt-4o' (main.py:30), a catalog id. Only one OpenAIHelper is built per deployment (main.py:111), so there is no per-user key.
